public.geolocation.purpose: Zip-code lookup with city, state, and coordinates for geographic joins

public.geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_.purpose: First digits of a postal code used as a stable location key
public.geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_.notes: Join key, not a display value. Never shown to end users.

public.geolocation.geolocation_lat.purpose: Latitude of the zip code centroid

public.geolocation.geolocation_lng.purpose: Longitude of the zip code centroid

public.geolocation.geolocation_city.purpose: City the zip code belongs to

public.geolocation.geolocation_state.purpose: State the zip code belongs to
public.geolocation.geolocation_state.notes: Ambiguous with customer_state and seller_state. See ambiguities.

public.customers.purpose: People or accounts that have placed at least one order

public.customers.customer_id.purpose: Per-order pseudo-identity linking a customer to their orders
public.customers.customer_id.notes: One physical person can have multiple customer_ids. Never expose raw.

public.customers.customer_unique_id.purpose: Stable identity of a physical person across accounts
public.customers.customer_unique_id.notes: Use this, not customer_id, for any 'unique customers' count.

public.sellers.purpose: Merchants who list and sell products on the marketplace

public.sellers.seller_id.notes: Never expose raw to end users.

public.orders.purpose: Confirmed purchases with a full lifecycle (approved → shipped → delivered)

public.orders.customer_id.purpose: The customer account that placed the order
public.orders.customer_id.notes: Join to customers on this. Not the same as customer_unique_id.

public.orders.order_status.purpose: Current lifecycle state of the order
public.orders.order_status.notes: Only 'delivered' counts as revenue. Never include 'shipped' or 'invoiced'.

public.orders.order_purchase_timestamp.purpose: When the customer placed the order
public.orders.order_purchase_timestamp.notes: All time-based questions default to this column unless stated otherwise.

public.orders.order_approved_at.purpose: When payment was approved for the order
public.orders.order_approved_at.notes: Null for orders that were never approved.

public.orders.order_delivered_carrier_da.purpose: When the order was handed to the carrier
public.orders.order_delivered_carrier_da.notes: Null for orders that never shipped.

public.orders.order_delivered_customer_d.purpose: When the order reached the customer
public.orders.order_delivered_customer_d.notes: Null for orders that were not delivered. The key column for delivery-time metrics.

public.orders.order_estimated_delivery_d.purpose: The date the customer was promised the order
public.orders.order_estimated_delivery_d.notes: Always present. Used for on-time vs late-delivery comparisons.

public.products.purpose: Product catalog with pricing, category, and physical dimensions

public.products.product_category_name.purpose: Business category the product belongs to

public.products.price.notes: Not the same as order_items.price, which is the actual transaction price.

public.products.selling_price.purpose: The price the product is currently sold at

public.products.product_name_lenght.purpose: Character length of the product name

public.products.product_description_leng.purpose: Character length of the product description

public.products.product_photos_qty.purpose: Number of photos attached to the product listing

public.products.product_weight_g.purpose: Shipping weight of the product in grams

public.products.product_length_cm.purpose: Length of the packaged product in centimeters

public.products.product_height_cm.purpose: Height of the packaged product in centimeters

public.products.product_width_cm.purpose: Width of the packaged product in centimeters

public.order_items.purpose: Individual line items within an order

public.order_items.order_id.purpose: The parent order this line belongs to

public.order_items.order_item_id.purpose: Sequence number of the line within the order
public.order_items.order_item_id.notes: Starts at 1 per order. Not globally unique on its own.

public.order_items.seller_id.purpose: The seller who fulfilled this line

public.order_items.shipping_limit_date.purpose: The deadline by which this line had to ship

public.order_items.price.purpose: Unit price of the item on this line
public.order_items.price.notes: Not the same as payment_value. Sums of this column do NOT equal revenue.

public.order_payments.purpose: Payment records for orders, possibly split across multiple rows

public.order_payments.order_id.purpose: The order this payment applies to

public.order_payments.payment_sequential.purpose: Sequence number of the payment within the order

public.order_payments.payment_installmen.purpose: Number of installments the payment was split into

public.order_payments.payment_value.purpose: Amount paid by this payment record
public.order_payments.payment_value.notes: Sum across an order equals the order's total. This is the column metrics use.

public.order_reviews.order_id.purpose: The order this review is about

public.order_reviews.review_comment_titl.purpose: Short headline the customer wrote for the review

public.order_reviews.review_comment_mess.purpose: Full text of the customer's review

public.order_reviews.review_answer_times.purpose: When the marketplace replied to the review

gmv.from_sql: order_payments op JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = op.order_id
gmv.notes: Use this, not SUM(order_items.price), for any 'revenue' question.

net_revenue.from_sql: order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
net_revenue.notes: Includes freight. Prefer gmv for headline revenue questions.

product_revenue.from_sql: order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id

freight_revenue.from_sql: order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id

aov.from_sql: order_payments op JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = op.order_id

units_sold.from_sql: order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id

unique_customers.notes: Use customer_unique_id, not customer_id. customer_id is per-order.

repeat_customers.from_sql:
(
  SELECT c.customer_unique_id
  FROM customers c
  JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 1
) rc

new_customers.from_sql:
(
  SELECT c.customer_unique_id
  FROM customers c
  JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) = 1
) nc

positive_review_rate.definition_sql: SUM(CASE WHEN r.review_score >= 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)

negative_review_rate.definition_sql: SUM(CASE WHEN r.review_score <= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)

late_delivery_rate.definition_sql: SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)

prior_quarter.sql: o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE_TRUNC('quarter', NOW()) - INTERVAL '3 months' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < DATE_TRUNC('quarter', NOW())

active_customer.sql:
c.customer_unique_id IN (
  SELECT c2.customer_unique_id
  FROM customers c2
  JOIN orders o2 ON o2.customer_id = c2.customer_id
  WHERE o2.order_purchase_timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '180 days'
)

lapsed_customer.sql:
c.customer_unique_id NOT IN (
  SELECT c2.customer_unique_id
  FROM customers c2
  JOIN orders o2 ON o2.customer_id = c2.customer_id
  WHERE o2.order_purchase_timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '180 days'
)

repeat_customer.sql:
c.customer_unique_id IN (
  SELECT c3.customer_unique_id
  FROM customers c3
  JOIN orders o3 ON o3.customer_id = c3.customer_id
  GROUP BY c3.customer_unique_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o3.order_id) > 1
)

new_customer.sql:
c.customer_unique_id IN (
  SELECT c3.customer_unique_id
  FROM customers c3
  JOIN orders o3 ON o3.customer_id = c3.customer_id
  GROUP BY c3.customer_unique_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o3.order_id) = 1
)

forbidden.rule: Never SELECT customer_id in output columns. Use customer_unique_id for counting.
Never SELECT seller_id in output columns.
Never SELECT order_id in output columns unless the question explicitly asks for a list of orders.
Never SELECT product_id in output columns unless the question asks for product identifiers.
Never SELECT review_id.
Never SELECT zip code prefix columns in output. They are join keys.
Never SELECT latitude or longitude. They are lookup values only.
Never SELECT raw review text unless the question asks for review content.
Only join tables within the public schema.
Never reference tables in the auth schema.
Never reference tables in the storage schema.
Never reference tables in the vault schema.
Never reference tables in the realtime schema.
Never reference tables in the extensions schema.
Never reference pg_catalog or information_schema.
'revenue' must resolve to the gmv metric definition.
SUM(order_items.price) is not revenue. Use gmv.
Revenue is a sum of amounts, not a count of orders.
gmv must always include order_status = 'delivered' in its WHERE clause.
'Unique customers' must use customer_unique_id, never customer_id.
Order counts must use COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), never COUNT(*).
Units sold must come from order_items, not orders.
AOV denominator must be COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), never COUNT(*).
Average review score must use AVG, never SUM.
Positive reviews are review_score >= 4, not >= 3.
Negative reviews are review_score <= 2, not <= 1.
Delivery time must use order_delivered_customer_date, not order_delivered_carrier_date.
Late delivery must compare delivered_customer_date to estimated_delivery_date.
Never emit a query that joins two tables without an ON clause.
Never join order_items to orders without matching on order_id.
order_payments must join to orders on order_id.
order_reviews must join to orders on order_id.
order_items must join to orders on order_id.
order_items must join to products on product_id.
order_items must join to sellers on seller_id.
customers must join to orders on customer_id, not customer_unique_id.
Never use COUNT(*) to count entities. Use COUNT(DISTINCT <pk>).
Every non-aggregate column in SELECT must appear in GROUP BY.
Never average an already-averaged value.
Never sum an already-averaged value.
Time filters must use order_purchase_timestamp unless the question names another date.
Never filter on orders with order_purchase_timestamp > NOW().
Current time must come from NOW(), not a hardcoded date.
Never emit SELECT *. Always project explicit columns.
Never add LIMIT unless the question asks for a bounded set.
Never hardcode a year. Use NOW() - INTERVAL or DATE_TRUNC.
Never emit CREATE, DROP, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or TRUNCATE.
Never emit SQL comments.

state.disambiguation: Default to customer_state unless the question mentions sellers or zip codes.

city.disambiguation: Default to customer_city unless the question mentions sellers or zip codes.

zip.disambiguation: Default to customer_zip_code_prefix unless the question mentions sellers or coordinates.

region.disambiguation: Default to customer_state unless the question is about sellers.

date.disambiguation: Default to order_purchase_timestamp unless the question names a lifecycle stage.

amount.disambiguation: Default to payment_value; use order_items.price only if the question says 'item price'; use freight_value only if it says 'shipping'.

delivery.disambiguation: Default to order_delivered_customer_date; use carrier_date only if the question mentions the carrier; use estimated_delivery_date only for promise comparisons.

payment.disambiguation: If the question asks 'how they paid', use payment_type. If 'how much', use payment_value. If 'how many times', use payment_installments.

product.disambiguation: If the question asks 'which product', use product_name. If it asks 'how many products', use product_id.

review.disambiguation: If the question asks about 'rating' or 'stars', use review_score. If about 'text', use review_comment_message.

customer.disambiguation: Default to customer_unique_id unless the question is about a specific order's customer record.

revenue.disambiguation: Default to gmv unless the question explicitly says 'net', 'product only', or 'including freight'.

customer key.disambiguation: Same identifier. Use customers.customer_id when the question is about the customer record; orders.customer_id when filtered by order.

seller key.disambiguation: Same identifier. Use sellers.seller_id for the merchant roster; order_items.seller_id for sales attribution.

order key.disambiguation: Same identifier. Anchor on orders.order_id for the canonical record; use the other tables' columns for joins.

product key.disambiguation: Same identifier. Use products.product_id for the catalog; order_items.product_id for sales.

item key.disambiguation: Same as 'product key'. Both refer to the same identifier.

list price.disambiguation: order_items.price is the transaction price; products.price is the catalog price. Default to order_items.price when the question is about an order.

order_status.disambiguation: Only one column; declared to document the value_map dependency.

category.disambiguation: Only one column; declared to document the value_map dependency.

score.disambiguation: Only one column; declared to document the value_map dependency.

name.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.

weight.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.

height.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.

width.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.

length.disambiguation: Default to product_length_cm; use the *_lenght columns only if the question is about text length.

purchase.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.

approval.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.

installment.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.

freight.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.

buyer.disambiguation: Only one meaningful column; declared to document the customer/customer_unique_id distinction.

merchant.disambiguation: Only one column; declared for completeness.
